transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I've been feeling incredibly restless lately and just can't seem to sit still. It constantly feels like I'm "on the go," almost as if I'm driven by a motor. It's getting really hard to manage, so I wanted to see if there's anything I can do about it.
Have you felt this restless and 'driven by a motor' for as long as you can remember, dating back to your childhood, or does it come and go in distinct periods?

I've actually felt this way since I was a kid, definitely before I turned 12, rather than it coming and going in phases. While I've felt restless and "driven by a motor" for as long as I can remember, it has been particularly persistent and noticeable for the last year and five months.
Along with this restlessness, do you also frequently struggle with paying attention, keeping organized, or forgetting things in your daily life?
No, I don't really struggle with paying attention, keeping organized, or forgetting things. My main issue is just this constant restlessness and feeling like I always have to be on the go.
Do you also find yourself constantly worrying excessively about many different everyday things, and finding it very hard to control those worries?

No, I don't really experience that kind of constant worrying. My mind doesn't get anxious or caught up in excessive worries about everyday things; it's really just my body that feels like it always needs to be moving.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder. The patient has confirmed that their physical restlessness has been present since childhood (before age 12) and denies excessive worry, which rules out Generalized Anxiety Disorder. They also deny inattentive symptoms, confirming the diagnosis of ADHD, Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation. No further candidates are needed, and the interview can be concluded.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits chronic, persistent symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity (feeling restless, unable to sit still, and 'driven by a motor') that began in childhood (before age 12). They deny significant symptoms of inattention or generalized anxiety, which rules out the Combined Presentation of ADHD and Generalized Anxiety Disorder, pointing directly to ADHD (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation).
